newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-HOYER-LARSEN RECOVERING FROM POST-OLYMPIC GLOW.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-HOYER-LARSEN RECOVERING FROM POST-OLYMPIC GLOW.

text.p: Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen is confident he has recovered from post-Olympic glow ahead of the All England badminton championships starting in Birmingham on Tuesday.
Hoyer-Larsen thrilled all Denmark but stunned much of Asia and beyond when he won the men's singles gold medal in Atlanta.

However, by his own admission it took months to get over the elation and he has not won an open tournament since the Games. "They were months when I should have been working (on his game) but did not," the Dane acknowledged.
The outcome was a disappointing time on the international circuit in the Far East and India and fears that Atlanta would be seen as the high-water mark.
But in the last couple of weeks Hoyer-Larsen has felt the confidence surging.

Now based in England, he has been working out at the national badminton centre with compatriot Thomas Stuer-Lauridsen and South Korean Park Joo-bong, the greatest doubles player of his time and now coaching for England.

The Birmingham championships are a high-profile, high-prestige event and when Hoyer-Larsen won there a year ago, reversing years of domination by such Asian powerhouses as Indonesia, China and Malaysia, he sounded a clear warning.
He starts favourite to retain his title and feels almost 100 percent ready to do himself justice with the rest to come in time for the world championships in May in Glasgow.
He starts in Birmingham with an easy-looking task against an unranked Dutchman and then seems likely to face ex-European and English champion, Darren Hall, a great national favourite over the years.
Malaysia's Rashid Sidek is seeded second ahead of former world champion Joko Suprianto of Indonesia and the talented Chinese Sun Jun.

Other top Indonesians on display include Heryanto Arbi, an ex world and All England winner, the 1992 Olympic champion Allan Budi Kusuma and old favourite Ardy Wiranata, a former All England winner and still a delight to watch.

The women's title should go to young Indonesian Mia Audina who is top seeded some way ahead of the sport's "first lady" Susi Susanti, ranked only joint five despite a brilliant record at these championships.

England's Jo Muggeridge will be hoping for a trouble free-tournament after a much publicised run-in with the country's director of elite play Steve Baddeley which ended with her pouring a can of soft drink over his head.
